FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Drawing Sectional Committee and approval by the Production and General Engineering Division Council 


(PGDO). 


This standard was first published in 1988. This revision has been taken up to incorporate feedback gained through 
experience and other developments taken at international level in this field. 


In the preparation of this standard assistance has been derived from DIN 30-5:2002 ‘Simplified Drawing — Part 5 
Foreign Part drawings, direction for preparing’ issued by the Deutsches Institut Für Normung (DIN). 


The use of foreign part drawings offers the following advantages depending upon the type of organizations: 


a) 


b) 
c) 
d) 


e) 


Explicit definition of non-standard commercial objects. In the event of insufficient clarity of supplier 
documents, any additions can be made to the foreign part drawing. 


Independent vis-à-vis the document of the supplier. 
Uniformity in documents for article numbering and repeat parts. 


Uniformity in documents, rendering shorter text in the purchaser order, since only the drawing name and 
drawing number need to be specified. 


Uniform and sufficient inspection documents for good inscript. 


Repeat part numbering may be at the discretion of the company/orgnizations. 


IS 12461 (Part 2) : 2017 


Indian Standard 


SIMPLIFIED PRESENTATION OF TECHNICAL 
DOCUMENTS 


(GUIDE FOR PREPARATION OF ORDER DRAWINGS 
FOR BOUGHT—OUT PARTS) 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard lays down the representation of foreign 
part drawings. This specifies the documentation of 
non-standard commercial objects for purchase 
purposes, which are mentioned in the documents of 
the supplier and are furnished with a manufacturer or 
supplier identification. These specifications are meant 
to ensure the supply of these parts in the required 
quality and with the required functions, in addition to 
achieving independence of later modifications 
performed to the documents of the supplier. 


2 REFRENCE 


The standards given below contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the edition 
indicated was valid. The standard is subject to revision, 
and parties to agreements based on this standard are 
encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying 
the most recent edition ofthe standard indicated below: 


IS No. Title 
IS 8930 Technical product documentation — 
(Part 1):1995 vocabulary Part 1 Terms relating to 
technical drawings: General and 
types of drawings 


3TERMS 


For the purpose of this standard definitions as given 
in IS 8930 (Part 1) shall apply. 


4 DIRECTIONS FOR PREPARING 


4.1 Foreign part drawings shall contain unique 
information suitable for ordering the objects and required 
for the assembly and inspection (see Fig. 1 to 3) 


4.2 Extracts from the documentation of the supplier, 
e.g. drawings, tables (see fig. 1 and 2) and test (see 
fig. 3) may, at times be incorporated in the 
representation of foreign part drawings. In the 
process, care shall be taken to ensure the compatibility 
and restorability of these extracts in the 


documentation process(data migration, software 
exchange). 


4.3 Where applicable, information by the customer (e.g. 
order number) shall be added to the tables extracted 
from the documents ofthe supplier (see tables in fig. 1 
and 2). Where required, the article code of the 
manufacturer may also be added to the table 


4.4 If necessary, manufacturer/supplier data as well 
as the title of the object shall be specified next to the 
title block or in appropriate supplementary fields (e.g. 
for citing of source for the content of the drawing). 
If a fixed supplier is specified for technical reasons, 
then the following shall be added: e.g. : "Supplier 


4.5 As far as possible, the name shall be derived from 
the commercial name of the objects and shall be 
specified in the title block. 


4.6 Details not specified in the foreign part drawing 
shall be regarded as customary in the trade and are 
indirectly specified in or above the title block with 
relevant information (see footnote “a” in Fig. 1) 


4.7 As a rule, foreign part drawings are not meant for 
own production, which is why this should be indicated 
at an appropriate information on the drawing plane, 
e.g. by the marking: "Foreign part drawing, 
manufacturer ...... e 


4.8 The proprieter (company or the manufacturer) of 
industrial property rights shall be specified in the 
foreign part drawings (see Fig. 1) 


5 MODIFICATIONS IN THE INFORMATION 
PROVIDEDIN THE DRAWING 


5.1 The information of the purchaser on the foreign 
part drawing takes procedure over the generally valid 
information provided by the manufacturer. This is in 
particular applicable in the event of modifications in 
the documents of the supplier.

Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


“BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: PGD 24 (1303).
